subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: Should OpenClaw expose Telegram custom emoji through raw `<tg-emoji>`/rich HTML only, or add a typed Telegram entity surface on the shared message tool and delivery payloads?
rationale: Both paths can represent custom emoji, but the issue now spans shared tool API, Telegram plugin internals, captions, replies, chunking, and fallback behavior; automation should not invent that public contract.

options.title: Approve a typed entity surface
options.body: Add a validated Telegram-owned `entities`/`caption_entities` contract through the message tool and delivery payloads while preserving existing `<tg-emoji>` HTML support.

options.title: Keep HTML/rich-only support
options.body: Declare raw `<tg-emoji>` and rich HTML as the supported public path and close or narrow entity-array requests separately.

options.title: Defer behind broader formatting policy
options.body: Handle this together with Telegram parse/render mode policy, accepting slower delivery but avoiding another public message-tool shape now.

recommendation.title: Approve a typed entity surface
recommendation.body: Add a validated Telegram-owned `entities`/`caption_entities` contract through the message tool and delivery payloads while preserving existing `<tg-emoji>` HTML support.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already framed the prior API-shape review on this issue and has relevant Telegram formatting history.
